explanation: The name goes back to an ancient Greek silver coin. A drachma was worth six obols, and its name meant a 'handful', perhaps from a fistful of six iron spits once used as money.

claims.text: Greece used the drachma until euro notes and coins replaced it in 2002.
The lira, the peseta and the escudo were the currencies of Italy, Spain and Portugal, not Greece.
The modern drachma was named after an ancient Greek silver coin.
In ancient Greece, one drachma was worth six obols.
The word drachma meant 'a handful', possibly from a handful of six iron spits (obols) used as early money.
